hints.title: What must be built
hints.body: You need a set of roads that connects every settlement without cycles. Such a set is a spanning tree, and the cheapest one is a minimum spanning tree.

hints.title: Every pair is a candidate
hints.body: The graph is complete: any two settlements can be joined, with cost equal to their Manhattan distance.

hints.title: Grow one tree
hints.body: Prim's algorithm starts from one settlement. Repeatedly add the unconnected settlement whose cheapest road to the current tree is smallest. Keep a `best` array instead of materializing every edge.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
best[0] = 0, all other best values = infinity
repeat n times:
    choose unvisited u with minimum best[u]
    mark u visited
    add best[u] to total
    for every unvisited v:
        best[v] = min(best[v], manhattan(u, v))
return total
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete implementation.
